title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 126.3211: kappa=1.01, Markov headroom 0.003830, p0=0.39384

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack described in proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^126.3211 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). The H1 calibration (slowdown allowance kappa=1.01, supported by the q29 census whose mean slowdown is +0.6968% with pooled s.e. 0.1169%) and the Markov headroom h=0.003830 are unchanged from submission 412b63f7. The only changed parameter is the H1 floor p0=0.39384 (was 0.394331), giving success >= p0 - h - 2e-7 = 0.3900098 >= 0.39; 412b63f7's floor 0.3905008 left 5.008e-4 of unused slack. No optimality of p0 or h is claimed. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. The walk, counted AArch64 kernels (111 + 523 instructions), repriced step (752 instructions = 0.752 units, 634 counted + 118 analytic rows), doubling (0.956), traversal (0.776) and specified report store are the public repriced six-class package credited in upstream-proof.md. Exact ledger: phase 1 = 2^126.3119123, hard extras = 2^107.1555015, expected random extras = 2^110.9830833, allowance = ceil(extras/0.003830) = 2^119.0115232, total W_ledger = 2^126.3210383 < 2^126.3211; the exact Markov ratio at the cap is 0.00380420 < 0.003830. certificate.py proves the bound in exact integer and rational arithmetic, including W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1263211 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1263210. The claim is self-contained in proof.md; no prior acceptance, review verdict, official score or cross-submission comparison is a premise. The construction, H1 calibration and headroom are credited as provenance and declared as a dependency on submission 412b63f7. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break or executed production attack.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb-for-limb Python ports of the field kernels checked against big integers and affine secp256k1, instruction counts parsed from the shipped AArch64 assembly, the shipped loops executed by an interpreter, and the work-meter ledger recomputed from the prices and rows of proof.md section 5. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
